commitments.quote: Business Associate may use and disclose PHI only as necessary to perform the Underlying Agreements, as required by law, or as permitted by this BAA.
commitments.summary: Business Associate may use or disclose PHI only to perform the Underlying Agreements, as required by law, or as this BAA permits.
commitments.scope: PHI that Business Associate creates, receives, maintains or transmits for Covered Entity under the Underlying Agreements.
commitments.deviation: The DPA limits processing to Customer's documented instructions. The BAA limits use and disclosure to performing the Underlying Agreements, legal requirements, or BAA permissions.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall limit its uses and disclosures of PHI to the minimum necessary.
commitments.summary: Business Associate must apply a minimum-necessary standard to its uses and disclosures of PHI.
commitments.scope: All PHI.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Business Associate may de-identify PHI only in accordance with the safe harbor method at 45 C.F.R. § 164.514(b)(2), and may use the de-identified information only to provide and improve the services under the Underlying Agreements.
commitments.summary: Business Associate may de-identify PHI only by the HIPAA safe harbor method and may use the result only to provide and improve services under the Underlying Agreements.
commitments.scope: De-identification of PHI and use of the de-identified information.
commitments.deviation: The DPA lets ExampleCo use aggregated or de-identified Usage Data to operate, secure and improve the Services. The BAA requires the HIPAA safe harbor method and limits use to providing and improving services under the Underlying Agreements, which excludes securing the services.

commitments.quote: Information de-identified in accordance with this Section 2.3 is not PHI and is not subject to this BAA.
commitments.summary: Information properly de-identified under the safe harbor method is not PHI and falls outside the BAA.
commitments.scope: Data de-identified under 45 C.F.R. § 164.514(b)(2) is excluded from BAA coverage.
commitments.deviation: The DPA excludes Usage Data, defined as aggregated or de-identified data that does not identify Customer or any person, from Customer Personal Data. The BAA excludes only information de-identified by the safe harbor method.

commitments.quote: A limited data set under 45 C.F.R. § 164.514(e) is PHI for all purposes of this BAA.
commitments.summary: A limited data set is treated as PHI and is fully covered by the BAA.
commitments.scope: Limited data sets under 45 C.F.R. § 164.514(e).
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall comply with Subpart C of 45 C.F.R. Part 164 with respect to ePHI.
commitments.summary: Business Associate must comply with the HIPAA Security Rule (Subpart C) for ePHI.
commitments.scope: ePHI.
commitments.deviation: The DPA requires the measures in Annex 2, which ExampleCo may update. The BAA requires compliance with the HIPAA Security Rule and lists no specific measures such as AES-256, TLS or MFA.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall not store, process or access PHI outside the United States.
commitments.summary: Business Associate may not store, process or access PHI outside the United States, which bars offshore support access.
commitments.scope: All PHI, covering storage, processing and access, including by Business Associate personnel.
commitments.deviation: The DPA stores data in the customer-selected region and allows access from outside it, including from Manila, Philippines. The BAA prohibits any storage, processing or access outside the United States. It names no exception for Subcontractors, so the ban appears to apply to them as well (inference).

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall maintain HITRUST r2 certification for the systems that store or process PHI.
commitments.summary: Business Associate must maintain HITRUST r2 certification for systems that store or process PHI.
commitments.scope: Systems that store or process PHI.
commitments.deviation: The DPA requires a SOC 2 Type II report and ISO/IEC 27001 certification for the Services. The BAA requires HITRUST r2 for PHI systems and does not mention SOC 2 or ISO 27001.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall report to Covered Entity any Breach of Unsecured PHI without unreasonable delay and in no event later than ten (10) calendar days after Discovery.
commitments.summary: Business Associate must report any Breach of Unsecured PHI without unreasonable delay and within 10 calendar days after Discovery.

deadline.anchor: Discovery of the Breach, as defined in the HIPAA Rules incorporated by Section 1.1 (the contract itself does not say whose knowledge counts)

commitments.recipient: Covered Entity's Privacy Office at privacy-office@ahs.example, with a copy to its Information Security Office at iso@ahs.example (Section 4.4)
commitments.scope: Breaches of Unsecured PHI. It is unconfirmed whether this period or the shorter 5-business-day period in 4.2 governs a Breach that is also a Security Incident, because the BAA has no precedence term (inference).
commitments.deviation: The DPA requires notice within 72 hours after ExampleCo confirms a Personal Data Breach. The BAA allows 10 calendar days after Discovery, which is longer, and covers Breaches of Unsecured PHI rather than confirmed breaches of Customer Personal Data.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall report to Covered Entity any Security Incident within five (5) business days after Business Associate becomes aware of it.
commitments.summary: Business Associate must report any Security Incident within 5 business days after it becomes aware.

deadline.anchor: Business Associate becomes aware of the Security Incident

commitments.recipient: Covered Entity's Privacy Office at privacy-office@ahs.example, with a copy to its Information Security Office at iso@ahs.example (Section 4.4)
commitments.scope: Security Incidents as defined in 45 C.F.R. § 164.304, limited to incidents involving ePHI that Business Associate or its Subcontractors create, receive, maintain or transmit for Covered Entity (Section 1.2).
commitments.deviation: The DPA has no separate security-incident reporting term and notifies only on a confirmed Personal Data Breach, within 72 hours. The BAA covers any Security Incident, including attempted ones, within 5 business days of awareness rather than confirmation.

commitments.quote: This Section 4.2 serves as notice of, and no further report is required for, unsuccessful attempts such as pings, port scans and blocked log-in attempts that do not result in unauthorized access to ePHI.
commitments.summary: The BAA itself serves as standing notice of unsuccessful attempts such as pings, port scans and blocked log-ins, so no individual reports are required for them.
commitments.scope: Unsuccessful attempts that do not result in unauthorized access to ePHI.
commitments.deviation: The DPA excludes unsuccessful attempts from the definition of Personal Data Breach, so they are never reported. The BAA treats them as Security Incidents but deems them notified through this Section.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall report to Covered Entity any use or disclosure of PHI not provided for by this BAA within ten (10) calendar days after becoming aware of it.
commitments.summary: Business Associate must report any use or disclosure of PHI not permitted by the BAA within 10 calendar days after becoming aware.

deadline.anchor: Business Associate becomes aware of the unauthorized use or disclosure

commitments.recipient: Covered Entity's Privacy Office at privacy-office@ahs.example, with a copy to its Information Security Office at iso@ahs.example (Section 4.4)
commitments.scope: Any use or disclosure of PHI not provided for by the BAA, whether or not it is a Breach.
commitments.deviation: The DPA has no equivalent for non-breach impermissible uses. It notifies only a confirmed Personal Data Breach, within 72 hours. The BAA gives 10 calendar days from awareness.

commitments.quote: Reports under this Section 4 shall be made in writing to Covered Entity's Privacy Office at privacy-office@ahs.example, with a copy to its Information Security Office at iso@ahs.example.
commitments.summary: All reports under Section 4 must be written and sent to the Privacy Office, with a copy to the Information Security Office.
commitments.recipient: Privacy Office at privacy-office@ahs.example, with a copy to the Information Security Office at iso@ahs.example
commitments.scope: Reports of Breaches, Security Incidents and impermissible uses or disclosures.
commitments.deviation: The DPA sends notice to the security contact designated in the admin console, or else the account owner. The BAA names two fixed email addresses and requires written reports with a copy to the Information Security Office.

commitments.quote: A report of a Breach shall include, to the extent known, the identity of each individual affected, the PHI involved, the date of the Breach and of its Discovery, and the steps taken to mitigate it.
commitments.summary: A Breach report must include, to the extent known, the affected individuals' identities, the PHI involved, the Breach and Discovery dates, and mitigation steps.
commitments.recipient: Covered Entity's Privacy Office at privacy-office@ahs.example, with a copy to its Information Security Office at iso@ahs.example (Section 4.4)
commitments.scope: Reports of Breaches only.
commitments.deviation: The DPA requires the nature of the breach, the categories of data and measures taken, plus further information as available. The BAA requires individual-level identities and dates, and states no express duty to supplement the report.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall reimburse Covered Entity's reasonable costs of notifying individuals, regulators and the media of a Breach caused by Business Associate or its Subcontractors.
commitments.summary: Business Associate must reimburse Covered Entity's reasonable costs of notifying individuals, regulators and media about a Breach it or its Subcontractors caused.
commitments.scope: Breaches caused by Business Associate or its Subcontractors.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall ensure that each Subcontractor that creates, receives, maintains or transmits PHI on its behalf agrees in writing to the same restrictions and conditions that apply to Business Associate under this BAA.
commitments.summary: Business Associate must obtain each PHI-handling Subcontractor's written agreement to the same restrictions and conditions as the BAA.
commitments.scope: Each Subcontractor that creates, receives, maintains or transmits PHI on Business Associate's behalf.
commitments.deviation: The DPA makes ExampleCo responsible for its Subprocessors' performance. The BAA requires written flow-down of the same restrictions. The BAA has no Subprocessor notice or objection mechanism like DPA 5.2 to 5.4, so any such rights are not stated in it.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall make PHI in a Designated Record Set available to Covered Entity within ten (10) business days after Covered Entity's request, so Covered Entity can meet 45 C.F.R. § 164.524.
commitments.summary: Business Associate must make PHI in a Designated Record Set available to Covered Entity within 10 business days of its request.

deadline.anchor: Covered Entity's request

commitments.scope: PHI in a Designated Record Set.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall make its internal practices, books and records relating to PHI available to the Secretary of Health and Human Services for purposes of determining compliance with the HIPAA Rules.
commitments.summary: Business Associate must make its internal practices, books and records relating to PHI available to the HHS Secretary to determine HIPAA compliance.
commitments.recipient: Secretary of Health and Human Services
commitments.scope: Internal practices, books and records relating to PHI.
commitments.deviation: The DPA allows an on-site audit only when a supervisory authority requires one, and gives customers SOC 2 and pen-test summaries. The BAA gives the HHS Secretary access to records, and contains no customer audit right or pen-test commitment.

commitments.quote: On termination of the Underlying Agreements, Business Associate shall return or destroy all PHI within thirty (30) days.
commitments.summary: On termination of the Underlying Agreements, Business Associate must return or destroy all PHI within 30 days.

deadline.anchor: termination of the Underlying Agreements

commitments.scope: All PHI.
commitments.deviation: The DPA deletes Customer Personal Data within 90 days, with a further 35 days for backups. The BAA requires return or destruction within 30 days, with no separate backup period and no deletion certification term (DPA 10.2).

commitments.quote: If return or destruction is not feasible, Business Associate shall extend the protections of this BAA to that PHI for as long as it retains it.
commitments.summary: If return or destruction is infeasible, Business Associate must keep applying the BAA's protections to the retained PHI for as long as it holds it.
commitments.scope: PHI for which return or destruction is infeasible.
commitments.deviation: The DPA has no infeasibility exception and requires deletion in all cases, with backups overwritten within 35 days. The BAA lets infeasible PHI be retained under continuing BAA protections.

commitments.quote: This VDPA prevails over the Subscription Agreement and over any data processing terms, policies or online terms of Vendor or its Affiliates.
commitments.summary: The VDPA overrides the Subscription Agreement and any data processing, policy or online terms of the Vendor or its Affiliates, so this VDPA's incident-notice and other duties control.
commitments.scope: Applies to all of the VDPA, including over terms of Vendor Affiliates such as ExampleCo, Inc., which is listed as a Subprocessor in Amendment No. 1 to Appendix B. Inference: the Vendor's standard DPA terms, such as a 72-hour breach notice, would not displace the 24-hour period in 6.1.
commitments.deviation: The baseline DPA controls over the Agreement only as to processing of Customer Personal Data. This VDPA prevails over the whole Subscription Agreement and over all Vendor and Affiliate data processing terms, policies and online terms.

commitments.quote: "Retailer Data" means all data that Retailer, its employees or its customers provide to Vendor or that Vendor collects from Retailer's systems, including telemetry, logs, traces and metrics, and all data derived from any of it.
commitments.summary: The data protected by this VDPA is all Retailer Data, including telemetry, logs, traces, metrics and anything derived from them, and is not limited to personal data.
commitments.scope: All data from Retailer, its employees or customers, or collected from Retailer's systems, plus all derived data. It is not limited to personal data.
commitments.deviation: The baseline covers only Personal Data contained in Customer Data. This contract covers all Retailer Data, including telemetry and derived data, whether or not it is personal.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall process Retailer Data only to provide the services described in the Subscription Agreement (the "Services") and on Retailer's written instructions.
commitments.summary: Vendor may process Retailer Data only to provide the Services and on Retailer's written instructions.
commitments.scope: All Retailer Data as defined in 2.2.
commitments.deviation: The baseline permits processing on documented instructions, including the customer's configuration of the Services. This contract requires written instructions and a purpose limited to providing the Services, and covers all Retailer Data.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall not use Retailer Data to train or improve any machine learning model, except models used only to provide the Services to Retailer.
commitments.summary: Vendor may not use Retailer Data to train or improve any machine learning model unless the model is used only to serve Retailer.
commitments.scope: Any machine learning model, including derived data under the Retailer Data definition. The only exception is models used solely for Retailer's Services.
commitments.deviation: The baseline bars only training or fine-tuning of foundation models made available to other customers, and allows use of aggregated Usage Data to improve the Services. This contract bars training or improving any ML model, with a narrow Retailer-only exception, and has no Usage Data carve-out.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall store Retailer Data only in the United States or Canada.
commitments.summary: Vendor must store Retailer Data only in the United States or Canada.
commitments.scope: Covers storage of Retailer Data. The contract does not say anything about remote access from other countries (inference: access from outside the US and Canada is not expressly restricted).
commitments.deviation: The baseline stores data in the hosting region the customer selects. This contract fixes storage to the US or Canada. It has no equivalent of the baseline's 6.2 permission to access data from outside the region, such as Manila.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall maintain administrative, technical and physical safeguards that meet or exceed the CIS Critical Security Controls, Implementation Group 2.
commitments.summary: Vendor must maintain safeguards meeting or exceeding CIS Critical Security Controls IG2.
commitments.deviation: The baseline commits to its own Annex 2 measures, which Vendor may update. This contract sets an external benchmark (CIS IG2) and has no unilateral update right.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall encrypt Retailer Data at rest and in transit using industry-standard encryption.
commitments.summary: Vendor must encrypt Retailer Data at rest and in transit using industry-standard encryption.
commitments.scope: All Retailer Data.
commitments.deviation: The baseline specifies AES-256 at rest and TLS 1.2 or higher in transit. This contract requires only unspecified industry-standard encryption.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall obtain a SOC 2 Type II report covering the Services each year and provide it to Retailer within fifteen (15) days after Retailer's request.
commitments.summary: Vendor must obtain a SOC 2 Type II report on the Services every year and give it to Retailer within 15 days of a request.

deadline.anchor: Retailer's request for the SOC 2 Type II report

secondary_deadline.anchor: Annual SOC 2 Type II report covering the Services

commitments.scope: SOC 2 Type II report covering the Services.
commitments.deviation: The baseline makes the report available through the Trust Center under NDA terms with no delivery deadline. This contract requires delivery to Retailer within 15 days of request. It does not mention ISO/IEC 27001 certification (baseline 4.2) or an annual penetration test (baseline 9.2).

commitments.quote: Vendor shall not permit any Subprocessor other than those listed in Appendix B to process Retailer Data without Retailer's prior written consent.
commitments.summary: Only Subprocessors listed in Appendix B may process Retailer Data unless Retailer gives prior written consent.
commitments.scope: Subprocessor includes any third party, including any Vendor Affiliate, that processes Retailer Data on Vendor's behalf (2.4).
commitments.deviation: The baseline gives general authorization to engage Subprocessors and publishes a list. This contract requires prior written consent for any Subprocessor not listed in Appendix B and expressly treats Vendor Affiliates as Subprocessors.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall request consent for a new Subprocessor in writing at least thirty (30) days before the Subprocessor begins processing Retailer Data. Retailer's silence is not consent.
commitments.summary: Vendor must ask for Retailer's written consent to a new Subprocessor at least 30 days before it starts processing, and silence does not count as consent.

deadline.anchor: New Subprocessor begins processing Retailer Data

commitments.scope: Any new Subprocessor, including a Vendor Affiliate.
commitments.deviation: The baseline gives 30 days' notice via the Trust Center with a 15-day objection right and termination as the sole remedy. This contract requires an affirmative written consent request, silence is not consent, and there is no urgent-replacement exception.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall bind each Subprocessor in writing to obligations at least as protective as this VDPA, and remains liable for each Subprocessor's acts and omissions.
commitments.summary: Vendor must bind each Subprocessor in writing to terms at least as protective as the VDPA and stays liable for their acts and omissions.
commitments.scope: Every Subprocessor, including Vendor Affiliates.
commitments.deviation: The baseline says ExampleCo remains responsible for Subprocessors' performance of the DPA obligations. This contract adds an express written flow-down requirement and liability for all Subprocessor acts and omissions.

commitments.quote: ExampleCo, Inc. (Vendor Affiliate) Platform hosting and AI features for the Services United States
commitments.summary: Amendment No. 1 (September 8, 2025) approves ExampleCo, Inc., a Vendor Affiliate, as a Subprocessor for platform hosting and AI features in the United States, alongside the originally listed AWS (hosting) and Helpdesk Platform, Inc. (support ticketing).
commitments.scope: ExampleCo is approved for platform hosting and AI features only, located in the United States. It remains bound by 3.2 (no ML training), 3.3 (US/Canada storage), 5.3 and the Data Incident duties, because Data Incident covers incidents at a Subprocessor.
commitments.deviation: The baseline publishes a Subprocessor list on the Trust Center under general authorization. This contract names approved Subprocessors in Appendix B, and the Affiliate was added by a specific amendment.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall notify Retailer of a Data Incident without undue delay and no later than twenty-four (24) hours after Vendor becomes aware of it.
commitments.summary: Vendor must notify Retailer of a Data Incident without undue delay and within 24 hours of becoming aware of it.

deadline.anchor: Vendor becomes aware of the Data Incident (actual or reasonably suspected); the contract does not say whose awareness counts beyond 'Vendor'

commitments.scope: Data Incident means any actual or reasonably suspected unauthorized access to, or acquisition, disclosure or loss of, Retailer Data, including while held by a Subprocessor.
commitments.deviation: The baseline gives 72 hours after ExampleCo confirms a Personal Data Breach. This contract gives 24 hours after awareness, covers reasonably suspected incidents and incidents at Subprocessors, and has no confirmation threshold or exclusion for unsuccessful attempts.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall send notice by email to Retailer Security Operations at secops@arg.example and by telephone to +1 (614) 555-0182. Notice to Retailer's account or procurement contacts does not satisfy Section 6.1.
commitments.summary: Incident notice must go by both email and telephone to Retailer Security Operations, and notice to account or procurement contacts does not count.
commitments.recipient: Retailer Security Operations, email secops@arg.example and telephone +1 (614) 555-0182
commitments.scope: Notice of Data Incidents under Section 6.1.
commitments.deviation: The baseline sends notice to the security contact designated in the admin console, or else the account owner. This contract requires both email and phone to named Security Operations contacts and rejects notice to account or procurement contacts.

commitments.quote: Vendor's notice shall describe the Data Incident, the Retailer Data involved, any Subprocessor involved, and the steps Vendor has taken. Vendor shall supplement the notice as new information becomes available.
commitments.summary: The incident notice must describe the incident, the data involved, any Subprocessor involved and steps taken, and Vendor must supplement it as new information emerges.
commitments.scope: Data Incidents as defined in 2.3.
commitments.deviation: Similar to the baseline, but this contract additionally requires identifying any Subprocessor involved, has no 'to the extent then known' qualifier, and sets no deadline for supplements.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall not inform Retailer's customers or any third party of a Data Incident involving Retailer Data without Retailer's prior written approval, except as required by law.
commitments.summary: Vendor may not tell Retailer's customers or any third party about a Data Incident without Retailer's prior written approval unless the law requires it.
commitments.scope: Data Incidents involving Retailer Data; the exception is disclosure required by law.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall cooperate with Retailer's investigation
commitments.summary: Vendor must cooperate with Retailer's investigation of a Data Incident.
commitments.scope: Retailer's investigation; the contract says nothing specific about evidence preservation, so this type is the closest fit (inference).
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: shall bear the reasonable costs of a Data Incident to the extent caused by Vendor or its Subprocessors.
commitments.summary: Vendor must pay the reasonable costs of a Data Incident to the extent it or its Subprocessors caused it.
commitments.scope: Reasonable costs, limited to the extent caused by Vendor or its Subprocessors.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Within thirty (30) days after the Subscription Agreement ends, Vendor shall delete all Retailer Data and confirm the deletion to Retailer in writing.
commitments.summary: Vendor must delete all Retailer Data within 30 days after the Subscription Agreement ends and confirm the deletion to Retailer in writing.

deadline.anchor: Subscription Agreement ends

commitments.scope: All Retailer Data, including derived data. No backup carve-out is stated.
commitments.deviation: The baseline gives 90 days plus 35 days for backups and provides certification only on request. This contract gives 30 days, states no backup extension, and requires written confirmation without a request.

commitments.quote: Retailer may audit Vendor's compliance with this VDPA once per calendar year on thirty (30) days' notice, and within ten (10) days after notice following a Data Incident.
commitments.summary: Retailer may audit Vendor's compliance once per calendar year on 30 days' notice, and also within 10 days after notice following a Data Incident.

deadline.anchor: Annual audit (Retailer's notice)

secondary_deadline.anchor: Retailer's notice of an audit following a Data Incident

commitments.scope: Audit of Vendor's compliance with the VDPA, once per calendar year plus a post-Data-Incident audit.
commitments.deviation: The baseline treats reports as satisfying audit rights, with one on-site audit only where a supervisory authority requires it, on 60 days' notice, at Customer's expense. This contract grants a direct annual audit on 30 days' notice and an additional post-incident audit, with no regulator trigger and no stated limits on hours or costs.

commitments.quote: This VDPA binds and benefits each party's successors and permitted assigns.
commitments.summary: The VDPA binds and benefits each party's successors and permitted assigns.
commitments.scope: Successors and permitted assigns of both parties.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: A change of control of Vendor, by merger, acquisition or otherwise, does not terminate or modify this VDPA. Any acquirer's standard terms do not apply to Retailer Data unless Retailer agrees in writing.
commitments.summary: A change of control of Vendor does not end or change the VDPA, and an acquirer's standard terms do not apply to Retailer Data without Retailer's written agreement.
commitments.scope: Any change of control of Vendor by merger, acquisition or otherwise; applies to all Retailer Data.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: This Addendum controls over any conflicting term of the Agreement, any order form, and any data processing addendum, privacy policy, or other document published or provided by Supplier.
commitments.summary: The Addendum overrides any conflicting term in the Agreement, order forms, any DPA, privacy policy or other Supplier document.
commitments.scope: Covers all Supplier documents, including any data processing addendum. This displaces the 72-hour breach term and other terms in a Supplier DPA to the extent they conflict.
commitments.deviation: The DPA says it controls over the Agreement for processing Customer Personal Data. Here the Bank's Addendum controls over the Agreement and over any Supplier DPA.

commitments.quote: Terms incorporated by reference to a Supplier website, including any Supplier trust or security site, do not bind Bank and do not modify this Addendum.
commitments.summary: Terms that exist only on a Supplier website or trust site do not bind the Bank or change the Addendum.
commitments.scope: Supplier websites and trust or security sites, including Trust Center subprocessor lists and notices.
commitments.deviation: The DPA gives subprocessor notice by updating the Trust Center list and emailing subscribers. Here Trust Center terms do not bind the Bank, so notice must follow Section 5.2 and Exhibit C.

commitments.quote: "Bank Data" means all data and information, in any form, that Supplier or any Subcontractor receives, accesses, creates or processes in connection with the Agreement, including (a) data provided by or on behalf of Bank or its customers; (b) metadata, logs and configuration data relating to Bank's use of the Services; and (c) any data derived from any of the foregoing, including model outputs, embeddings, annotations, and data that has been aggregated, de-identified, pseudonymized or tokenized.
commitments.summary: Bank Data covers all data in any form connected to the Agreement, including metadata, logs, derived data, model outputs, and aggregated or de-identified data.
commitments.scope: Defines the data that triggers the Addendum's security, location, AI, incident and deletion duties. Aggregated or de-identified data is expressly included.
commitments.deviation: The DPA covers only Personal Data in Customer Data, and its Usage Data (aggregated or de-identified) falls outside protection. Here Bank Data is much broader and includes aggregated, de-identified, pseudonymized and derived data.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall maintain a written information security program that is consistent with the NIST Cybersecurity Framework and the FFIEC Information Technology Examination Handbook.
commitments.summary: Supplier must keep a written security program consistent with NIST CSF and the FFIEC IT Handbook.
commitments.deviation: The DPA commits to the Annex 2 measures, which Supplier may update. Here Supplier must maintain a written program aligned to named frameworks (NIST CSF, FFIEC).

commitments.quote: Supplier shall encrypt Bank Data at rest using AES-256 or stronger and in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher.
commitments.summary: Supplier must encrypt Bank Data at rest with AES-256 or stronger and in transit with TLS 1.2 or higher.
commitments.scope: Bank Data, as broadly defined in Section 2.2.
commitments.deviation: The encryption standards match Annex 2. Here the duty covers all Bank Data, a broader category than Customer Data.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall require multi-factor authentication for all remote access to systems that store, process or transmit Bank Data.
commitments.summary: Supplier must require multi-factor authentication for all remote access to systems that handle Bank Data.
commitments.scope: All remote access to systems that store, process or transmit Bank Data.
commitments.deviation: The DPA requires MFA for access to production systems. Here MFA applies to all remote access to any system that handles Bank Data.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall complete a criminal background check on all Supplier Personnel before granting them access to Bank Data, to the extent permitted by law.
commitments.summary: Supplier must complete criminal background checks on all personnel, including Subcontractor personnel, before granting access to Bank Data, where law permits.

deadline.anchor: granting Supplier Personnel access to Bank Data

commitments.scope: Supplier Personnel, defined to include employees, contractors and agents of Supplier and of any Subcontractor.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent. The DPA requires only written confidentiality obligations for personnel (Section 3.1).

commitments.quote: Supplier shall maintain throughout the term of the Agreement a current SOC 2 Type II report covering the Services.
commitments.summary: Supplier must keep a current SOC 2 Type II report covering the Services throughout the term.
commitments.scope: The Services, for the term of the Agreement.
commitments.deviation: The DPA also commits to ISO/IEC 27001 certification or an equivalent. Here only SOC 2 Type II is required and ISO 27001 is not mentioned.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall store and process Bank Data only within the United States.
commitments.summary: Supplier must store and process Bank Data only in the United States.
commitments.scope: Bank Data, covering both storage and processing, including by Subcontractors.
commitments.deviation: The DPA stores data at rest in the customer-selected region and allows access from elsewhere. Here both storage and processing are limited to the US.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall not permit any Supplier Personnel located outside the United States to access Bank Data, including for support or maintenance, without Bank's prior written approval.
commitments.summary: No personnel outside the US may access Bank Data, even for support or maintenance, without the Bank's prior written approval.
commitments.scope: Supplier Personnel, which includes Subcontractor personnel, located outside the United States.
commitments.deviation: The DPA permits access from outside the hosting region, including from Manila, for support, maintenance and security. Here offshore access is prohibited without prior written Bank approval.

commitments.quote: Supplier may permit only the Subcontractors listed in Schedule 2 ("Approved Subcontractors") to access Bank Data, and each only within the scope stated for it in Schedule 2.
commitments.summary: Only the Schedule 2 Approved Subcontractors may access Bank Data, and only within their stated scope.
commitments.scope: Subcontractor is defined to include any third party, including Supplier Affiliates, that performs Services or has access to Bank Data.
commitments.deviation: The DPA gives general authorization to engage Subprocessors. Here only listed Subcontractors are permitted, each limited to its stated scope.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall give Bank's Third-Party Risk Management office at least ninety (90) days' prior written notice, delivered as provided in Exhibit C, before adding or replacing any Subcontractor or expanding an Approved Subcontractor's scope.
commitments.summary: Supplier must give the Bank's TPRM office at least 90 days' prior written notice before adding or replacing a Subcontractor or expanding an approved scope.

deadline.anchor: adding or replacing any Subcontractor or expanding an Approved Subcontractor's scope

commitments.recipient: Bank Third-Party Risk Management office, email tprm-notices@anb.example, with a copy to Awesome National Bank, N.A., Legal Department, 100 Example Plaza, New York, NY 10001 (Exhibit C)
commitments.scope: Adding or replacing any Subcontractor, and expanding an Approved Subcontractor's scope. There is no emergency-replacement exception in the text.
commitments.deviation: The DPA requires 30 days' notice by Trust Center update and email. Here notice must be 90 days, written, and sent to the TPRM office with a copy to Legal. The DPA's urgent-replacement exception (5.4) has no counterpart.

commitments.quote: Bank may object within thirty (30) days after receiving the notice. If Bank objects, Supplier shall not engage the Subcontractor for the Services provided to Bank, or Bank may terminate the affected Services without penalty and receive a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees.
commitments.summary: Bank may object within 30 days of notice. If it does, Supplier must not use the Subcontractor for Bank, or Bank may terminate the affected Services without penalty and get a pro-rata refund.

deadline.anchor: Bank's receipt of the Subcontractor notice

commitments.scope: Any new or replacement Subcontractor, or scope expansion, notified under Section 5.2. The objection need not be on stated grounds.
commitments.deviation: The DPA allows objection within 15 days on reasonable data protection grounds, with termination as the sole remedy after 30 days of failed resolution. Here the objection window is 30 days, no grounds are required, and the Subcontractor is barred for Bank or Bank may terminate with a pro-rata refund.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall impose on each Subcontractor written obligations at least as protective of Bank Data as this Addendum.
commitments.summary: Supplier must flow down written obligations to each Subcontractor that are at least as protective of Bank Data as the Addendum.
commitments.scope: Each Subcontractor, including Supplier Affiliates.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent. The DPA has no flow-down clause and states only that ExampleCo remains responsible (5.5).

commitments.quote: Supplier shall require each Subcontractor to notify Supplier of any Security Incident within six (6) hours after the Subcontractor's Discovery.
commitments.summary: Supplier must require each Subcontractor to notify Supplier of any Security Incident within 6 hours after the Subcontractor's Discovery.

deadline.anchor: Subcontractor's Discovery (the earliest time the Subcontractor knew, or with reasonable diligence would have known, of the Security Incident)

commitments.scope: Security Incidents at or involving any Subcontractor, including suspected incidents. This period binds the Subcontractor, not Supplier's notice to the Bank.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent. The DPA sets no Subprocessor-to-ExampleCo notice period.

commitments.quote: Supplier remains fully liable to Bank for the acts and omissions of its Subcontractors.
commitments.summary: Supplier stays fully liable to the Bank for the acts and omissions of its Subcontractors.
commitments.scope: All Subcontractors, including Supplier Affiliates.
commitments.deviation: The DPA makes ExampleCo responsible for Subprocessors' performance of DPA obligations. Here liability covers all acts and omissions.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall notify Bank of any Security Incident as soon as possible and in no event later than twelve (12) hours after Discovery.
commitments.summary: Supplier must notify the Bank of any Security Incident as soon as possible and within 12 hours after Discovery.

deadline.anchor: Discovery: the earliest time Supplier or any Subcontractor knew, or by exercising reasonable diligence would have known, of the Security Incident

commitments.recipient: Bank Cyber Fusion Center: telephone (24x7) +1 (212) 555-0147; email cfc-thirdparty@anb.example (Exhibit C)
commitments.scope: Any actual or reasonably suspected Security Incident, including unauthorized access to Bank Data or to any Supplier or Subcontractor system that stores, processes or transmits Bank Data, whether or not access to Bank Data is confirmed. This is the controlling period under Section 6.8, being shorter than the 72-hour period in Exhibit D.
commitments.deviation: The DPA gives 72 hours after ExampleCo confirms a Personal Data Breach. Here the limit is 12 hours from Discovery, which includes constructive knowledge and Subcontractor knowledge, and covers suspected incidents and unconfirmed access.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall give notice under Section 6.1 by telephone and by email to Bank's Cyber Fusion Center as provided in Exhibit C. Notice provided only to Bank's relationship manager, or through a Supplier status page or trust site, does not satisfy Section 6.1.
commitments.summary: Incident notice must be given by both telephone and email to the Bank's Cyber Fusion Center, and notice only to the relationship manager or via a status or trust page does not count.
commitments.recipient: Bank Cyber Fusion Center: telephone (24x7) +1 (212) 555-0147; email cfc-thirdparty@anb.example (Exhibit C). The relationship manager (Dana Okafor) is for routine matters only.
commitments.scope: Notices under Section 6.1.
commitments.deviation: The DPA sends notice to a customer-designated security contact or the account owner. Here notice goes by phone and email to the Bank's Cyber Fusion Center, and other channels do not satisfy the duty.

commitments.quote: Supplier's initial notice shall include all information then known about the Security Incident, including the date and time of Discovery, the systems and Subcontractors involved, and the categories of Bank Data affected or potentially affected.
commitments.summary: The initial notice must include everything then known, including date and time of Discovery, systems and Subcontractors involved, and categories of Bank Data affected or potentially affected.
commitments.scope: Initial notice of a Security Incident.
commitments.deviation: The DPA requires the nature of the breach, categories of data affected and measures taken, to the extent known. Here the notice must include all information then known, the Discovery time, the systems and Subcontractors involved, and potentially affected data.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall provide written status updates at least once every twenty-four (24) hours until the Security Incident is contained
commitments.summary: Supplier must give written status updates at least every 24 hours until the Security Incident is contained.

deadline.anchor: initial notice, repeating until the Security Incident is contained

commitments.recipient: Bank (inference: the Cyber Fusion Center, since Exhibit C does not name a recipient for updates)
commitments.scope: Security Incidents until containment.
commitments.deviation: The DPA says only that further information will be provided as it becomes available, with no fixed interval. Here updates are written and due at least every 24 hours.

commitments.quote: shall deliver a written root-cause report within thirty (30) days after containment.
commitments.summary: Supplier must deliver a written root-cause report within 30 days after containment.

deadline.anchor: containment of the Security Incident

commitments.scope: Security Incidents.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall not notify any Bank customer, regulator, law enforcement agency or the media of a Security Incident involving Bank Data without Bank's prior written consent, unless required by law. Where law requires such notice, Supplier shall inform Bank before giving it, to the extent legally permitted.
commitments.summary: Supplier may not notify Bank customers, regulators, law enforcement or the media about an incident without the Bank's prior written consent unless law requires it, and must tell the Bank first where legally permitted.

commitments.recipient: Bank (prior written consent, or advance notice where law requires)
commitments.scope: Security Incidents involving Bank Data. The restriction yields to legal requirements.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent. The DPA has no restriction on third-party communications.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall preserve all logs, images and other forensic evidence relating to a Security Incident for at least one (1) year after containment, and shall give Bank and its designated forensic investigator access to that evidence on request.
commitments.summary: Supplier must preserve all forensic evidence for at least one year after containment and give the Bank and its forensic investigator access on request.

deadline.anchor: containment of the Security Incident

commitments.recipient: Bank and its designated forensic investigator
commitments.scope: Logs, images and other forensic evidence relating to a Security Incident.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.scope: Security Incidents caused by Supplier or any Subcontractor.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent. The DPA has no cost reimbursement term, and Section 7.4 says notification is not an admission of fault.

commitments.summary: Supplier's obligations to ANB Securities LLC are supplemented by Exhibit D.
commitments.scope: ANB Securities LLC, which is an Affiliate of the Bank.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.deviation: The DPA has no shortest-period rule and fixes a single 72-hour period. Here the shortest applicable period governs.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall not use Bank Data to train, fine-tune, evaluate or improve any artificial intelligence or machine learning model, other than a model used solely to provide the Services to Bank.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall not permit any person to review, label or annotate Bank Data for the purpose of developing or improving any model, except as expressly permitted for an Approved Subcontractor in Schedule 2.

commitments.quote: Bank, its auditors and its regulators may audit Supplier's compliance with this Addendum once in any twelve (12) month period on thirty (30) days' written notice, and at any time after a Security Incident on five (5) business days' written notice.

commitments.summary: Supplier must test the BC/DR plan at least annually, give the Bank a summary of the results, and join the Bank's annual resilience exercise on 60 days' notice.

commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Within thirty (30) days after termination of the Agreement or Bank's written request, Supplier shall return Bank Data to Bank in the format Bank reasonably requests and then securely destroy all Bank Data, including in backups, held by Supplier and its Subcontractors.
commitments.summary: Within 30 days after termination or the Bank's written request, Supplier must return Bank Data in the requested format and then securely destroy all of it, including backups and Subcontractor-held copies.

commitments.summary: Within 10 business days after destruction, Supplier must deliver a certificate of destruction signed by an officer.

commitments.summary: Helpdesk Platform, Inc. may access only the contact details of Bank users for support ticketing.
